5 - P.N.G. Axar 2/2: [What are the food options like in Japan?] There are Indian restaurants here, and we are getting packed food from them and eating that. But yes, we are getting food. There are three or four good Indian restaurants, and they make good food, so we are having packed food from them. But it's very good. Obviously, cricket isn't played that much in Japan, but I think the job they are doing is very commendable. In terms of the ground and the atmosphere, I think they are doing a very good job within their capabilities. And in the coming years, I think it will be upgraded and they will provide even better conditions (for cricket). [How has your Games Village experience been so far?] I think the first experience has been very good. It's a different experience. Earlier, when we travelled with the team to Australia, England and other places, it was a different experience. But being here with (other) athletes during these Games, and coming here to play at the Asian Games, you know, everyone has an ID card, and people look at you differently when they see it because they know you are an athlete. It's the first time I've experienced something like this. Even when you are walking around, if you have an ID card, people look at you differently and think, "Oh, he's an athlete." So that's been a different experience. [What would winning gold for India mean personally?] If you win gold, it's a different experience. Yes, we have won the World Cup and other tournaments, but when you play for India, obviously, when you play with the BCCI, you are also playing for India. But this is different because you are being awarded a gold medal and you have come to play for your country at the Asian Games. It's a new experience, and I think it's very important. The way we are playing our cricket, I think we have a good chance of winning gold, and it's a very good opportunity. For me, it would be a very proud moment. Axar Patel 1/2: [Did Sri Lanka have any chance to beat India?] I mean, they had to do it to win, so we did what we had to do. But yeah, obviously, we had been waiting for quite a few days to play. You know, it was raining and the matches weren't happening, but kudos to the team because when the match happened, I think everyone was switched on. To put in such a performance after a long break, I think everyone did a very commendable job overall. [On the total posted by India batting first] I think Pakistan and Bangladesh also played on the same wicket, so we had seen that and estimated that 140-150 could be a winning total. So when we got 160 (169), we thought we were somewhere around 10-15 runs above par. When the match started, we were thinking 140-150. The way things were happening in the first match, and the ball was moving with drift, turn and bounce, we felt that 140 to 150 would be a winning score. [Will India-Pakistan gold-medal clash be played on the same pitch?] No, so far we don't have any idea which wicket the final will be played on. We had spoken about it, but it hasn't been confirmed yet. But as you have seen, the venue has three wickets, and all three wickets are similar, with cracks on them. So I think they will behave similarly, whichever wicket we play on. Whether we play on the adjacent wicket or the same wicket, I think it will behave similarly. 16:02 Local Time, 07:02 GMT, 12:32 IST: Absolute dominance from the Indians. Sri Lanka were a no-match for this Indian team. Ishan Kishan played a blinder on a tough pitch where the ball was misbehaving quite a bit. 169 was well above par. And the bowlers had a blast. Bumrah set the tone early with two wickets in the first over. Sri Lanka wanted to swing themselves to glory, but only ended up offering wickets to the Indian spinners. Axar, and Abhishek got two each while Washi got one. India will now face Pakistan for the Gold Medal, while Sri Lanka will play Bangladesh for the Bronze Medal. 9.5 W Abhishek Sharma to Binura Fernando, out Bowled!!
